blocks

blocks.text: S1 — assistant rows render blocks (closes task-e8ca8c5b9f99e9f8)

items.value: Assistant rows with a non-empty blocks array render through renderBlockNative under a new 'chat' typography register; rows without blocks fall back to plain source_markdown text exactly like the TUI's renderAssistantDoc fallback.

blocks.text: S2 — the six chat-* renderers + an honest role taxonomy (new task)

items.value: Hand-port chat-tool-diff, chat-todo, chat-thinking, chat-approval, chat-question, chat-plan into a new apps/mobile chat.tsx sibling of blocks.tsx, mirroring traversal semantics of js/packages/react/src/blocks/chat.ts — the established pattern (blocks.tsx:1-13 states it: RN sibling mirrors semantics, not DOM output). Fold at the shared 20-line budget behind a touch fold (LayoutAnimation + selection haptic — t3code's one usable collapse lesson); colors are the ok/danger role pair, NOT a new diff token family (design/tokens.json has none, and Studio+TUI both reuse status roles).

Replace the numberOfLines={3} italic systemLine (ChatSessionScreen.tsx:253-258) with the TUI's dispatch: assistant→blocks, tool/todo/thinking→typed block else one dim provenance line, approval/question/plan→CardRow (answerability stays on the message envelope — blocks never carry request_id, D35), unknown→render source. blocks.text: What we learned — including what the papers got wrong

children.value: The premise of mobile-paper lesson 1 is wrong for this house.

content.value: It recommends an RN markdown component; its own do-not-copy list (one renderer, no double pipeline, protect mermaid) argues for the blocks path instead. The corrections dossier and the upstream storm probes sharpened this into measured facts:

items.value: The tgz-pin 'vendoring technique' is INERT (correction C4): pnpm ignores overrides in a workspace-member package.json; t3code's lockfile resolves nitro-markdown 0.5.8 from the registry, not their vendored 0.5.0 tarball. Never copy it.

t3code's selection premium is narrower than advertised: t3-markdown-text is a real UITextView-backed Fabric module, but iOS-ONLY (Android hardcodes hasNativeSelectableMarkdownText() => false and falls to plain <Markdown>), selection breaks into islands at every code block / table / image (containsRichBlock, nativeMarkdownText.ts:661-713), and there is no custom context menu — just the OS default.

t3code left streaming performance on the table: nitro-markdown SHIPS a stable-prefix, fence-aware incremental parser (MarkdownStream, isInsideFencedCodeBlock) and their app uses none of it — full re-parse of the whole string per delta. Our Studio stable-boundary discipline is ahead of the thing the papers proposed stealing from.

Collapse lessons split (correction C20): #4409 is default-collapse of large diffs (already Barkpark law — the 20-line budget on three surfaces); #4475 is only a MANUAL collapse-all toggle. The steal reduces to 'extend the existing law to the third surface'; the toggle earns no slice (no surface has demanded it).

The block-attr source of truth is components.ex (:667-784), NOT chat_tool_renderer.ex — that file is the Studio-live renderer twin sharing pure helpers by defdelegate. A mobile spec citing chat_tool_renderer.ex for attrs cites the wrong file.

'system' is not a persisted role. Exactly 8 roles ever hit chat_messages (user, assistant, tool, todo, thinking, approval, question, plan); Studio's system banners are socket-local ephemera. The mobile fallback design targets tool-rows-without-blocks, not a phantom role.

react's chat-thinking label diverges from Go/Elixir ('thought for ~N tokens' lowercase+tilde vs '✻ Thought for N tokens'); mobile should adopt the Go/Elixir wording and the divergence should be fixed in react rather than adding a fourth variant.

The 20-line fold budget exists as four hand-synced constants (chat_tool_renderer.ex:62, components.ex:665, chat_blocks.go:41, chat.ts:125). Mobile adds a fifth — the golden fixture in S2 is the drift tripwire.

Diff colors: design/tokens.json has NO diff tokens by design — Studio uses var(--ok)/var(--danger)(+ -soft tints), the TUI uses generated ToneOK/ToneDanger. Mobile declares diff rows as ok/danger role reuse; minting values is lane 5's call (mobile's theme.ts is hand-authored hex, disconnected from the manifest — a lane-5 fact both Papers state the same way).

blocks.text: Risks & unknowns

items.value: Settled-turn 'pop': the tail re-layouts from plain text to formatted blocks at the turn boundary. The TUI ships this today; t3code/ChatGPT render markdown live. Mitigated by S3; whether the pop is acceptable for the next wave is a USER taste call.

Text selection: RN's selectable Text is weaker than a native UITextView. Honest gap — but measured smaller than feared: t3code's alternative is iOS-only, island-broken at rich blocks, OS-default menu. Do not oversell either side.
No syntax highlighting in house code blocks (plain mono) vs t3code's async shiki swap — a later JS-only premium slice, explicitly out of S1/S2.

The register touches blocks.tsx shared with the paper reader. Verified low-risk (private helper, no style assertions, zero snapshots) — but the jest pin is mandatory, and the 165 baseline is static-derived; run the suite once before citing it in acceptance criteria.

A fifth copy of the 20-line budget and a fifth implementation of the block visuals can drift; the golden fixture is the tripwire, and react's independent diff engine is prior evidence the risk is real.

Studio's HTML bodies for chat-thinking/approval/question/plan were not read (components.ex past ~:800) — the Studio column of the parity table is inferred for those four; a builder should glance before pixel-matching chip styles.
Timing: whether mobile can fetch a tool row BEFORE its output/task_id metadata merges land is unverified (matters to lane 2's work-log grouping, not to S1/S2 row rendering).

One Rendering Law, Third Surface

The premium transcript for the phone is not a markdown-library decision. The chat wire already delivers server-converted PortableDoc blocks for every rich row — assistant prose, tool diffs, todos, thinking, approval/question/plan cards — and the Studio and the Go TUI already render them under one shared law. Mobile is the only surface that ignores the blocks field it already receives, stores, and types. This Paper argues the rival rendering shapes to a verdict, designs the three build slices, and hands task-e8ca8c5b9f99e9f8 a decision-ready acceptance shape. It is one of five lane Papers feeding the crown: /papers/t3code-upgrade-capstone.

ADOPT the house path: render the server's PortableDoc blocks through mobile's existing renderBlockNative with a chat typography register, then port the six typed chat-* block renderers. Tri-surface parity by construction, zero new dependencies.

The rivals, argued to a verdict

Three shapes survived the T3 papers into this lane. The evidence decides two of them; the third survives only as a stretch.

OptionWhat it isVerdictWhy
(a) RN markdown component — t3code's path: nitro-markdown / t3-markdown-textParse source_markdown client-side per turnREJECTEDSecond markdown pipeline (violates the no-double-pipeline law); new native dep; forks mobile off the Studio/TUI golden-parity seam; loses MermaidIsland diagrams (t3code has zero mermaid anywhere). Storm verified the steal is weaker than the papers claimed: their selection module is iOS-only with selection islands at every code block/table, and their app never wires nitro-markdown's own incremental streaming API — it re-parses the full string per delta (SelectableMarkdownText.ios.tsx:42-59).

Pure rendering code, nothing else moves.
(c) Scoped hybrid — light inline formatting for the streaming tail, blocks for settled turnsStable-boundary tail formatting on top of (b)STRETCH (S3)Two-phase plain-tail is already house law (render.go D8/D9/D10) — the acceptable floor. Studio's stable-boundary discipline (chat_live.ex:5779+) is the proven premium tail; porting it is a taste call the user sequences, not a correctness need.

The decisive fact both T3 papers missed: this is not a build-a-renderer problem, it is a finish-the-third-surface problem. The storm confirmed the law holds all the way up: Studio's settled assistant turns render through render_paper_html/1 which IS FromMarkdown.blocks() |> Render.render_blocks(%{style: :article}) (chat_live.ex:5928-5934, called from replay :5031, live append :1385, and the streaming stable boundary :5799) — one engine, never a cached HTML string. What we will create — three slices

S1 — assistant rows render blocks (closes task-e8ca8c5b9f99e9f8)

  • Assistant rows with a non-empty blocks array render through renderBlockNative under a new 'chat' typography register; rows without blocks fall back to plain source_markdown text exactly like the TUI's renderAssistantDoc fallback.

S2 — the six chat-* renderers + an honest role taxonomy (new task)

The floor is the shipped two-phase law: plain streaming tail, blocks at the turn boundary (render.go D8/D9/D10 — a plain tail trivially cannot flicker, satisfying the task's no-flicker criterion). Amended acceptance shape for task-e8ca8c5b9f99e9f8

The task's current brief ('evaluate a minimal parser vs a small dep') is obsolete — the server already parses. Amend the three criteria to:

1. Assistant turns with blocks render native PortableDoc via renderBlockNative

Sequencing with lane 5 is explicit: the token/register values land first or in the same wave-slice; S1 consumes them. Both Papers state this identically.

What we learned — including what the papers got wrong

The premise of mobile-paper lesson 1 is wrong for this house. It recommends an RN markdown component; its own do-not-copy list (one renderer, no double pipeline, protect mermaid) argues for the blocks path instead.   • The tgz-pin 'vendoring technique' is INERT (correction C4): pnpm ignores overrides in a workspace-member package.json; t3code's lockfile resolves nitro-markdown 0.5.8 from the registry, not their vendored 0.5.0 tarball. Never copy it.
  • t3code's selection premium is narrower than advertised: t3-markdown-text is a real UITextView-backed Fabric module, but iOS-ONLY (Android hardcodes hasNativeSelectableMarkdownText() => false and falls to plain <Markdown>), selection breaks into islands at every code block / table / image (containsRichBlock, nativeMarkdownText.ts:661-713), and there is no custom context menu — just the OS default.
  • t3code left streaming performance on the table: nitro-markdown SHIPS a stable-prefix, fence-aware incremental parser (MarkdownStream, isInsideFencedCodeBlock) and their app uses none of it — full re-parse of the whole string per delta. Our Studio stable-boundary discipline is ahead of the thing the papers proposed stealing from.
  • Collapse lessons split (correction C20): #4409 is default-collapse of large diffs (already Barkpark law — the 20-line budget on three surfaces); #4475 is only a MANUAL collapse-all toggle. The steal reduces to 'extend the existing law to the third surface'; the toggle earns no slice (no surface has demanded it).
  • The block-attr source of truth is components.ex (:667-784), NOT chat_tool_renderer.ex — that file is the Studio-live renderer twin sharing pure helpers by defdelegate. A mobile spec citing chat_tool_renderer.ex for attrs cites the wrong file.
  • 'system' is not a persisted role. Exactly 8 roles ever hit chat_messages (user, assistant, tool, todo, thinking, approval, question, plan); Studio's system banners are socket-local ephemera. The mobile fallback design targets tool-rows-without-blocks, not a phantom role.
  • react's chat-thinking label diverges from Go/Elixir ('thought for ~N tokens' lowercase+tilde vs '✻ Thought for N tokens'); mobile should adopt the Go/Elixir wording and the divergence should be fixed in react rather than adding a fourth variant.
  • The 20-line fold budget exists as four hand-synced constants (chat_tool_renderer.ex:62, components.ex:665, chat_blocks.go:41, chat.ts:125). Mobile adds a fifth — the golden fixture in S2 is the drift tripwire.
  • Diff colors: design/tokens.json has NO diff tokens by design — Studio uses var(--ok)/var(--danger)(+ -soft tints), the TUI uses generated ToneOK/ToneDanger. Mobile declares diff rows as ok/danger role reuse; minting values is lane 5's call (mobile's theme.ts is hand-authored hex, disconnected from the manifest — a lane-5 fact both Papers state the same way).
